url: /kuda/tutorials/getting-started.md
---
# Getting started

Go from a checkout to a queryable, freshness-tracked memory of the
repo — the artifact an agent loads before planning instead of
re-exploring from scratch.

## Install

The `kuda` command is a tamias pack (`libraries/kuda`): a generated
`bins[]` shim → `tamias-driver-kuda` → the engine lib. There is no
cargo-installed `kuda` binary. With `tamias` installed:

```sh
tamias install 9aia:kuda@<version>    # org registry (needs TAMIAS_REGISTRY_TOKEN)
```

Or from a checkout of this repo:

```sh
scripts/pack.sh                                  # stage the driver payload
tamias install --allow-drivers ./libraries/kuda   # deploys `kuda`
```

## 1. Init

```sh
cd your-repo
kuda init
```

This writes a commented `kuda.toml` and a `.kuda/` skeleton. Open
the toml — the defaults are fully local and deterministic:

```toml
[extract]
kinds = ["manifest", "treesitter", "records"]   # adapter names, tried in order

[summarize]
kind = "template"                    # deterministic cards

[store]
kind = "sqlite"
path = ".kuda/index.sqlite"

[cards]
dir = ".kuda"                         # index.yaml + modules/*.yaml
```

The seeded file also carries commented `[repo]`, `[domains]`,
and `[workspace]` tables — the defaults are fully local and
deterministic.

If `rust-analyzer` is on PATH you can add `"lsp"` to `kinds` —
extraction quality tiers up automatically (see
[extraction tiers](/explanation/architecture#extraction-tiers)).

## 2. Sync

```sh
kuda sync
```

Output:

```
sync /home/you/your-repo
indexed 19 module(s) at 3432d05
```

`sync` walks manifests, runs the tree-sitter symbol queries from
`data/langs/*`, summarizes each module into a card, and stores the
symbol/edge graph in sqlite. It writes:

| path                   | tier | commit?                   |
| ---------------------- | ---- | ------------------------- |
| `.kuda/index.yaml`     | L0   | yes — the always-load card |
| `.kuda/modules/*.yaml` | L1   | yes — reviewable in diffs  |
| `.kuda/index.sqlite`   | L2   | no — rebuildable graph     |
| `.kuda/meta.json`      | meta | no — provenance record     |

## 3. Look at what it learned

```sh
kuda map
```

The L0 card: repo name, the module list, detected commands, and the
provenance block (`commit_sha`, file hashes, generator). This is the
\~1k-token blob an agent reads first.

```sh
kuda card kuda-store
```

An L1 card: purpose (from the manifest `description`), public API
symbols, dependency edges, `verify:` — the files to open before
trusting the card — and its own provenance.

## 4. Query

```sh
kuda find IndexStore
```

```
crates/kuda-store/src/lib.rs:9 Trait kuda-store
```

```sh
kuda dependents serde
```

```
kuda-cards --PackageDep--> serde
kuda-core --Imports--> serde
```

And the doc-sweep query — everything that mentions a name, useful
when a change must update code *and* docs and comments:

```sh
kuda refs SqliteStore --docs
```

## 5. Break it, then watch kuda notice

Edit any `crates/*/Cargo.toml` — change a `description` — and:

```sh
kuda status
```

```
drifted  kuda-store
19 fresh, 1 drifted (HEAD af26b8c)
```

`status` re-hashes each card's `verify:` files and compares with the
recorded provenance. `kuda sync` regenerates only what drifted.

## What you now know

* `init` scaffolds `kuda.toml` + `.kuda/`; extraction, summarization,
  and storage are config-swappable adapters.
* `sync` produces three tiers: L0 `index.yaml`, L1 `modules/*.yaml`
  (committed, reviewable), L2 `index.sqlite` (rebuildable).
* `map`/`card` read cards; `find`/`dependents`/`refs` query the
  symbol graph.
* `status` detects drift by re-hashing `verify:` files against
  recorded provenance; `sync` repairs incrementally.

You have built a committed, queryable, self-checking map of the
repository. Point agents at it — via `kuda mcp` or `kuda acp` — and
they plan against the map instead of grepping blindly.

## Where next

* **How-to** (tasks): [multi-repo](/how-to/multi-repo) ·
  [mcp](/how-to/mcp) · [acp](/how-to/acp) ·
  [llm summarizer](/how-to/llm-summarizer)
* **Reference** (lookup): [cli](/reference/cli) ·
  [config](/reference/config) · [crate api](/reference/crate-api)
* **Explanation** (why): [architecture](/explanation/architecture) ·
  [release model](/explanation/release-model) ·
  [comparison](/comparison) — vs grep / RAG

# How-to: index a multi-repo workspace

For sibling checkouts — an org of repos that import each other —
kuda keeps one index per repo *and* answers cross-repo questions
over all of them.

## 1. Declare the workspace

Create `.kuda/workspace.yaml` in the checkout you run `kuda`
from — either a repo's own `.kuda/` or a shared parent dir that
holds the sibling repos:

```yaml
roots:
  - kuda
  - mimus
  - ../cli
  - ../lsp
```

Paths resolve relative to the directory that owns the `.kuda/`
(the root `kuda` treats as cwd) — *not* the yaml's own directory.
Roots listed there replace the single-repo default; add `.` if
you want the home repo indexed too. One caveat: `--workspace`
loads the config of the directory you run from and applies it to
every root — sibling repos' own `kuda.toml` files are not
consulted, so keep per-root differences in the shared config or
run `kuda sync` per repo instead.

`[workspace] resolve_git_deps = true` in `kuda.toml` is the only
workspace key the config file honors — it maps `git = "…"`
manifest deps onto sibling checkouts (see step 4).

## 2. Sync all roots

```sh
kuda sync --workspace
```

```
sync /home/you/GitHub/9aia/kuda
indexed 19 module(s) at af26b8c
sync /home/you/GitHub/9aia/mimus
indexed 15 module(s) at 323421e
```

Each root gets its own `.kuda/` artifacts — the per-repo indexes
stay independent and committable in their own repos.

## 3. Query across the set

```sh
kuda dependents kuda-core --workspace
```

Edges found in *every* root's store are merged — so an import of
`kuda-core` inside `mimus` shows up alongside internal users.
That is the impact-analysis query that matters for a breaking
change: "who calls this, anywhere in the org".

## 4. Git dependency edges

`resolve_git_deps = true` records the intent for the extractor
tier that maps `git = "…"` manifest dependencies onto sibling
checkouts — turning "depends on github.com/x/y" into "depends on
the sibling repo y". Until that lands, cross-repo edges come from
module-name matching across the merged stores.

## Current limits

* `find` and `refs` remain per-root; `dependents` is the merged
  query today.
* Cards are generated per root — there is no aggregate workspace
  card yet. Compose one from `kuda map` output across roots.

url: /kuda/how-to/mcp.md

# How-to: serve the index over MCP

`kuda mcp` exposes the index as tools to MCP-capable agents
(Devin, Cursor, Claude Code, Zed, …). It is a stdio JSON-RPC
server — no ports, no daemon.

## Run

```sh
cd your-repo
kuda mcp
```

## Tools

| tool          | query                                   |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `repo_card`   | L0 blob — the always-load summary       |
| `module_card` | L1 card + freshness for one module      |
| `find`        | symbol -> file:line                     |
| `dependents`  | reverse dep edges (impact analysis)     |
| `refs`        | code + docs/comments mentions           |
| `status`      | provenance drift vs HEAD                |

## Register with your agent

stdio servers are declared in the client's MCP config — the shape
varies, but it is always "command + args":

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kuda": { "command": "kuda", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
```

Run it from a repo that has been `kuda sync`'d — the tools read
`.kuda/` at call time, so a re-`sync` is picked up without
restarting the server.

## Verify the handshake

```sh
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"find","arguments":{"name":"IndexStore"}}}' \
  | kuda mcp
```

Two replies: the `initialize` result, then a `content[0].text`
body like `crates/kuda-store/src/lib.rs:9 Trait kuda-store`.

## Trust model

Cards are hypotheses. Every `module_card` response includes the
`verify:` file list — agents should open those files before
acting on card content, and `status` tells them whether the whole
index has drifted. See [architecture](../explanation/architecture.md#trust-model).

See also: [ACP surface](acp.md) — same index, the other wire
protocol.

---

---
url: /kuda/how-to/acp.md
---
# How-to: the ACP surface

`kuda acp` speaks the Agent Client Protocol — the editor↔agent
wire protocol used by Zed and supported by agent clients such as
cline and Cursor. Where `kuda mcp` exposes *tools*, `kuda acp`
exposes the index as an *agent* you can prompt.

## Run

```sh
cd your-repo
kuda acp     # stdio JSON-RPC server
```

## Prompts

The session/prompt method accepts compact query strings:

| prompt              | returns                                  |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `find <symbol>`     | `file:line kind module` hits             |
| `dependents <name>` | reverse dep edges                        |
| `card <module>`     | the module card YAML                     |
| `map` / `status`    | the L0 card (fallback for anything else) |

Replies stream back as session/update notifications with
`agent_message_chunk` content, then a `stopReason: end_turn`
result.

## Verify

```sh
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"session/new","params":{"cwd":"'"$PWD"'","mcpServers":[]}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"session/prompt","params":{"sessionId":"kuda-default","prompt":[{"type":"text","text":"find IndexStore"}]}}' \
  | kuda acp
```

You get `agentInfo`, a `sessionId`, an `agent_message_chunk`
carrying `crates/kuda-store/src/lib.rs:9 Trait kuda-store`, and
`end_turn`.

## Which protocol when?

* **MCP** — the agent already has tool-use wired and you want the
  index as callable tools. Most current clients.
* **ACP** — you want kuda to appear as an *agent* inside an
  ACP-speaking client, sharing its own session model.

Both read the same `.kuda/` artifacts — pick per client, or run
both.

# How-to: add a language

Per-language knowledge is data, not code. A new language means a
new `data/langs/*.toml` descriptor — the extractors' vocabulary
stays fixed.

## The descriptor

`data/langs/rust.toml` is the template:

```toml
name = "rust"
extensions = [".rs"]
manifests = ["Cargo.toml"]          # module-boundary markers
grammar = "rust"                    # adapter id — see below

# Tree-sitter symbol query. Captures are @name.<kind> where
# <kind> maps to SymbolKind: function|type|trait|const|module|macro.
symbol_query = '''
(function_item name: (identifier) @name.function)
(struct_item name: (type_identifier) @name.type)
...
'''
```

| field          | used by                                  |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `name`         | reports, LSP `languageId`, dep normalization |
| `extensions`   | both extractors' file walking            |
| `manifests`    | package graph + module attribution       |
| `grammar`      | `kuda-extract-treesitter` language registry      |
| `symbol_query` | optional; falls back to a builtin        |
| `dep_query`    | optional; import edges for `dependents`  |

## What the adapter id controls

`grammar` is looked up in the adapter's registry — the match arm
inside `kuda-extract-treesitter::language()`. Today that registry has
`rust`, `typescript`, `python`, and `go`. Adding a grammar needs
the compiled `tree-sitter-<lang>` crate as a dependency plus one
arm — an adapter change, not an engine change. Descriptors for
languages without a compiled grammar still get `manifest`
extraction (module graph) for free.

## Writing a symbol query

1. Find the grammar's `node-types.json` (in the grammar repo) for
   the node names your language uses.
2. Capture the *name* child of each public-ish item as
   `@name.<kind>` — the kind suffix must match `SymbolKind`
   names or it lands in `Other`.
3. Test locally: put the query in `symbol_query`, run
   `kuda sync`, then `kuda find <a-symbol>`.

## Writing a dep query

`dep_query` captures the *import specifier* as `@dep` — whatever
syntax names the thing being imported (a `dotted_name`, a string
literal, a use-path root). Other captures in the same match are
ignored, so `#eq?` predicates can capture freely.

Sync normalizes each capture per language (`python` takes the
first dotted segment, typescript strips `./` relative specifiers
and keeps `@scope/pkg`, go keeps the full import path) and
rewrites it to a module name when it matches an indexed package
under `-`/`_` folding — `import neuralmind_shared` produces an
edge on `neuralmind-shared`. Unmatched specifiers stay external
(`dependents serde` still lists importers).

## Deploying descriptors

The CLI embeds `data/langs/*.toml` at build time. Adding a file
there + rebuilding is the whole distribution path today — a
config point for user-supplied descriptor dirs is a TODO item.

# How-to: index a record corpus

Non-code corpora — task ledgers, ADRs, handoffs — are record
collections the index can see. Domain knowledge is data, not code:
a new corpus means a new `data/domains/*.toml` descriptor — the
`records` extractor's vocabulary stays fixed (ADR-0003).

Enable it (on by default):

```toml
[extract]
kinds = ["manifest", "treesitter", "records"]
```

A corpus that doesn't exist on disk is a silent skip — enabling
`records` on a repo with no matching roots costs nothing.

## The descriptor

`data/domains/myco.toml` is the template:

```toml
name = "myco"
roots = ["project"]               # corpus dirs, repo-relative
extensions = [".md"]              # record files
module = "project"                # card + provenance grouping
purpose = "myco work ledger — tasks, ADRs, issues, plans, handoffs"

record_patterns = [
  # frontmatter: id = "ADR-0001" / item = "T-027"
  "(?:id|item)\\s*=\\s*\"([A-Z]+-[0-9]+)\"",
  # ledger lines: "- [ ] T-001" and "- T-013"
  "-\\s*(?:\\[[ xX]\\]\\s*)?([A-Z]+-[0-9]+)",
]
ref_pattern = "\\b[A-Z]+-[0-9]+\\b"
```

| field             | controls                                              |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `roots`           | dirs walked for records — worktree `.git`-file markers don't stop declared roots (omit for non-tree sources) |
| `extensions`      | which files are scanned (unused by non-tree sources)  |
| `source`          | non-tree corpus location — see [Non-tree sources](#non-tree-sources) |
| `module`          | the card the corpus gets (`kuda card <module>`)        |
| `purpose`         | card purpose (domain modules have no manifest/README) |
| `record_patterns` | per-line regexes; capture group 1 = the record id     |
| `ref_pattern`     | every match becomes a `references` dep-edge target     |

## How records become index entries

Each `record_patterns` match emits a `record`-kind `Symbol` —
`kuda find T-001` resolves to `file:line`. Frontmatter records and
checklist lines are the same mechanism: the pattern is the format
knowledge, not the parser.

`ref_pattern` matches emit `record -> id` edges —
`kuda dependents ADR-0001` answers "which tasks/docs reference
this". Edge scope: a file with one record scans the whole text; a
ledger with many records scopes each record's refs to its own
line, so `- [ ] T-002 blocked on T-001` edges `T-002 -> T-001`
without cross-wiring the whole file. If the pattern has a capture
group, group 1 is the edge target — `"`(ident)`"` strips the
backticks. Fenced code blocks never produce records; mentions
inside them still produce edges.

Corpus files bucket under `module` in the shared walk — the card,
its `verify:` file list, `status` drift, and incremental sync all
ride the existing pipeline.

## Edges into the code graph

`ref_pattern` targets resolve through the same `resolve_module`
pass as code deps — a task line naming `kuda-store` edges
`T-XXX -> kuda-store`, and `kuda dependents kuda-store` lists the
task alongside `PackageDep` edges. Under `--workspace`, the
resolution set is the **union of all roots' modules**: repo A's
`import sister_lib` lands on repo B's canonical `sister-lib`
module. One graph, federated stores — queries already merge
across roots, so cross-repo edges answer normally.

Shipped descriptors: `myco` (`project/` worktrees), `docs`
(`docs/` markdown — H1 headings as records, backticked
identifiers as edges), `media` (`file_records` mode — a record
per binary file), and `sturn` (non-tree — the coordination WAL
in git refs).

## Non-tree sources

A corpus doesn't have to live in the file tree. `[source]`
declares a non-filesystem corpus; today that's `sturn-wal` —
sturn's coordination WAL in git refs (`data/domains/sturn.toml`):

```toml
name = "sturn"
module = "sturn-wal"
purpose = "sturn coordination WAL — claims, writes, snaps, review events in refs/sturn/*"

record_patterns = ['"record":\s*"([^"]+)"']
ref_pattern = '"(?:path|from|to|glob|subject|event|ask|actor|ws)":\s*"([^"]+)"'

# [source] must come LAST: TOML nests every key after a table
# header inside that table, so a misplaced [source] would swallow
# the patterns into itself.
[source]
type = "sturn-wal"
ref_prefix = "refs/sturn"        # wal + archive refs
```

sturn keeps one ref per workspace — `refs/sturn/wal/<ws>`
(archives at `refs/sturn/archive/<ws>` on compaction) — each a
chain of commits whose tree holds one `event.json`. The
`records` extractor reads each ref as a **virtual JSONL file**:
one event per line, the ref name as `Symbol.file`, the event's
position as `Symbol.line`. The ordinary per-line record/edge
scan then applies unchanged — a WAL ref is just a multi-record
file that happens not to exist on disk.

Two fields are injected into each event line before scanning:
`seq` (1-based entry offset) and `record` — the queryable id
`<actor>:<op>@<ws>#<id8>` (`id8` = event/commit hash, stable
across compaction; `seq` is not). The descriptor's
`record_patterns` captures `record`, so `kuda find luis`,
`kuda find claim`, and `kuda find devin-wal-corpus` all land on
events, while `ref_pattern` edges each event to its payload —
`kuda dependents luis` lists an actor's ops, `kuda dependents
"crates/*"` finds claims on a glob.

Incremental sync works because each ref is registered as a
module input whose "content hash" is the ref's head sha: a
moved ref diffs exactly like a file write. A repo without
matching refs gets no module and no work — silent skip, same
as an absent corpus dir; `kuda doctor` reports `sturn` with
`(corpus absent)` there.

## Schema validation

Descriptors can carry `schema_json` — a JSON Schema (draft
2020-12) applied to frontmatter-bearing corpus files (`+++`
toml / `---` yaml). Regex finds records; the schema verifies
them:

```toml
schema_json = '''
{ "anyOf": [{"required": ["id"]}, {"required": ["item"]}],
  "properties": {
    "id":    {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[A-Z]+-[0-9]+$"},
    "status": {"enum": ["open", "claimed", "in-progress", "done"]} } }
'''
```

Invalid records stay indexed — they exist — but land as
warnings everywhere the card travels: `kuda sync` prints them,
`kuda card <module>` carries a `warnings:` field (so MCP's
`module_card` and the ACP surface see them too), `kuda status`
reports an invalid-record count, and `kuda doctor` reports
descriptor + schema compile health per domain. Files with no
frontmatter skip silently — line-records can't be schema'd.

## Try it

```sh
kuda sync
kuda card project        # the corpus card: api = record ids
kuda find T-001          # file:line of the record
kuda dependents ADR-0001 # what references this record
```

## Writing your own descriptor

Point `roots` at any dir of uniform-format record files, write a
`record_patterns` regex whose group 1 is the stable id, and set
`ref_pattern` to match that id shape. For a shared built-in, ship
it as a `data/domains/*.toml` and add it to `DOMAIN_TOMLS` in
`crates/kuda-cli/src/lib.rs`. For a repo-local corpus, declare it
in `kuda.toml` instead — no engine change needed. For a corpus
that isn't files at all, declare a `[source]` (see
[Non-tree sources](#non-tree-sources)) — new source types are an
engine change, new corpora of an existing type are data.

## Repo-local descriptors and disabling built-ins

`kuda.toml` can carry descriptors inline via `[[domain]]` — the
same fields as `data/domains/*` — and skip built-ins by name via
`[domains].disable`:

```toml
[domains]
disable = ["media"]        # built-ins: myco, docs, media

[[domain]]
name = "myco"              # same name as a built-in -> replace it
roots = ["ops/project"]
extensions = [".md"]
module = "ops-ledger"
purpose = "ops ledger"
record_patterns = ['-\s*(?:\[[ xX]\]\s*)?([A-Z]+-[0-9]+)']
ref_pattern = '\b[A-Z]+-[0-9]+\b'
```

Resolution is deterministic: built-ins load first, `disable`
names drop out, then `[[domain]]` entries apply in declared
order — a `name` matching a built-in replaces it (the repo wins),
any other name appends. The resolved set is what `sync`,
`status`, and `doctor` use — `kuda doctor` lists it with per
descriptor health, so a bad regex or schema in an inline entry
surfaces the same way a shipped one would.

url: /kuda/how-to/sturn.md
---
# How-to: sturn WAL integration

When a repo is [sturn](https://9aia.com/sturn/)-managed, kuda reads
the write-ahead log and feeds its ops into sync's diff — a typed,
evented change feed on top of the hash walk.

## What it does

`sync` already diffs by hashing every file. On sturn repos it
additionally walks `refs/sturn/wal/*` and marks modules touched by
these ops:

| op | feeds |
|---|---|
| `write` | `path` |
| `rename` / `delete` | `from` / `to` / `path` |
| `claim` / `release` | static prefix of `glob` |

Each ref's consumed head is persisted in the index (`sturn_wal:*`
meta keys), so ops are consumed exactly once.

**No config.** No WAL refs = no work. It's purely additive — a
write that bypassed sturn is still caught by the hash diff.

## Setup

```console
$ sturn init            # repo gets refs/sturn/wal/*
$ sturn ws create main  # a workspace to write through
$ kuda sync             # WAL ops now feed the diff
```

## The agent contract (advisory)

Agents should write *through* sturn when they can — claim before
editing, record intent — but sturn is **metadata, not a write
gate**. An agent that uses plain `write_file` doesn't break
anything; its change still lands in the hash diff, only the
coordination signal (claim/intent) is lost.

Point agents at sturn's MCP surface in their rules:

```markdown
## Writes
- Prefer `sturn` MCP tools for file writes: claim the path,
  write, then snap. Intent text is required.
- If sturn is unavailable, write normally — the index stays
  correct either way.
```

## Why additive, not exclusive

The WAL is ground truth *only* for writes that flowed through it.
The filesystem is ground truth for everything. kuda consumes both:
sturn says *who touched what and why*; hashes say *what actually
changed*. Neither is trusted alone.

---
# How-to: summarizers

`kuda-cards` turns extractions into the committed YAML artifacts.
Two shipping adapters: `template` (deterministic) and `acp`
(agent-written prose); `llm` is parked — ACP is the semantic path.

## `acp` — agent-written cards

```toml
[summarize]
kind = "acp"
acp_cmd = "env CLINE_PROVIDER=cline-pass CLINE_MODEL=cline-free/mimo-v2.6-flash cline --acp"
# NOTE: provider/model are env vars, not CLI flags — -P/-m are
# ignored in ACP mode.
```

`sync` spawns the agent once per run (one session, reused across
modules) and sends each module a session/prompt asking for
`purpose:`/`invariants:`/`notes:` grounded in the file list. The
agent's prose fills the card's `purpose` + `notes` regions —
`api`/`deps`/`verify`/`provenance` stay mechanical.

Protocol notes:

* session/request_permission from the agent is auto-answered
  with the first option — required, or the prompt deadlocks
* Any ACP-capable agent works: `cline --acp`, `zed agent`,
  `gemini --experimental-acp`, `devin acp`, …
* Prefer lightweight, no-tool agents for batch summarization:
  heavyweight clients work but pay for a full agent stack per
  spawn (`devin acp` boots the entire client + MCP servers), and
  the card prompt needs no tools — a fast text model is enough
* Reasoning-first agents may stream chain-of-thought ahead of the
  reply — kuda drops `agent_thought_chunk` updates and reads only
  the reply's final `purpose:`/`invariants:`/`notes:` block, so
  monologue never reaches the card
* Auth lives in the agent — kuda holds no keys
* Agent failure → silent `template` fallback per module

## `template` (default, shipping)

Deterministic, zero-model. Each module card's `purpose` comes
from the manifest `description` field (Cargo.toml
`[package].description`, package.json `description`); `api` lists
the extracted public symbols; `deps` lists the module's edges;
`verify:` lists the files the card was built from.

Because it is mechanical, `template` output is stable — the same
inputs always produce the same card, so diffs mean real change.
That is the property you want in committed, reviewed artifacts.

## `llm` (parked)

A direct-provider adapter (`provider`/`model` + keyring) is in
the backlog — ACP is preferred because it is agent-agnostic and
key-free. Same grounding rules apply when it lands: cite files or
stay silent, never clobber `verify:` or human `notes:`.

## Incremental sync

`sync` compares each module's input-file hashes with the committed
card's `provenance.hashes` before calling the summarizer — identical
means the card is reused and the agent is never prompted. Change one
file and only that module re-summarizes; the agent spend is
per-drift, not per-sync.

## File-tier cards

`file_cards = true` under `[summarize]` adds a finer L1 granularity: every
source file gets a `.kuda/files/<module>/<file>.yaml` card. Files
are split into ~1.5k-char semantic chunks (tree-sitter aware via
text-splitter), budgeted to ~14k chars per prompt, and each card
carries its own blob hash — an unchanged file never re-prompts.

# Command-Line Help for `kuda`

This document contains the help content for the `kuda` command-line program.

A hippocampus for your codebase — repo memory: index, query, verify

**Command Overview:**

* [`kuda`↴](#kuda)

## `kuda`

A hippocampus for your codebase — repo memory: index, query, verify

**Usage:** `kuda [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Commands:**

* `init` — Detect languages -> kuda.toml + .kuda/ scaffold
* `sync` — Incremental index (hash -> extract -> summarize -> store)
* `status` — Provenance vs HEAD: per-card drift report
* `map` — Render the L0 repo card (the always-load blob)
* `card` — Module card + freshness
* `find` — Symbol -> file:line
* `dependents` — Reverse dep lookup — impact analysis
* `refs` — Code + docs/comments mentions — the doc-sweep query
* `watch` — Watch the repo — fs events trigger incremental syncs (debounced; only changed modules re-summarize). Domain corpus roots are watched explicitly, so record writes (myco verbs, doc edits) re-index like code writes
* `mcp` — Serve the index over MCP (stdio)
* `acp` — Speak ACP — Agent Client Protocol surface for any agent client (zed, cline, cursor)
* `doctor` — Extractor/store/config health

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (else $KUDA_CONFIG, ./kuda.toml, ~/.config/kuda/kuda.toml)
* `--workspace` — Workspace mode — all roots in .kuda/workspace.yaml
* `-h, --help` — Print help
* `-V, --version` — Print version

# Config — `kuda.toml`

## Top level

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `RepoCfg` | optional | — |
| `extract` | `ExtractCfg` | optional | — |
| `summarize` | `SummarizeCfg` | optional | — |
| `store` | `StoreCfg` | optional | — |
| `cards` | `CardsCfg` | optional | — |
| `domains` | `DomainsCfg` | optional | — |
| `domain` | `descriptor table` | optional | `[[domain]]` inline domain descriptors — same shape as `data/domains/*`. A `name` matching a built-in replaces it (repo wins); others append. `[domains] domain` is the nested equivalent — both feed the resolved set. |
| `workspace` | `WorkspaceCfg` | optional | — |

## `[repo]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | optional | Defaults to the directory basename. |
| `root` | `path` | optional | Repo root; default = the toml's dir. |

## `[extract]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kinds` | `list` | optional | Impl kinds tried in order: "manifest" | "treesitter" | "lsp" | "records". |
| `lsp_server` | `string` | optional | Server command for the lsp adapter (per-language later). |
| `exclude` | `list` | optional | Extra dir/file names skipped during walks — beyond the built-in noise set (`default_excludes`). Keeps generated, vendored, and build output out of index, hashes, and agent prompts (agent cost is per-file fed in). |

## `[summarize]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `string` | optional | "template" (deterministic, default) | "acp" (agent-spawned). "llm" is a backlog adapter — ACP is the semantic path. |
| `acp_cmd` | `string` | optional | ACP agent command for kind="acp" — spawns per summarize. |
| `file_cards` | `bool` | optional | L1 per-file cards — chunked agent summaries per source file. Opt-in: ~10-50x the prompt count of module cards, bounded by per-file hash-skip. |
| `provider` | `string` | optional | Provider id for the llm adapter; key resolves via secrets chain. |
| `model` | `string` | optional | — |

## `[store]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `string` | optional | — |
| `path` | `path` | optional | L2 index path — rebuildable, gitignored. |

## `[cards]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `path` | optional | Committed artifacts dir: index.yaml + modules/\*.yaml. |

## `[domains]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disable` | `list` | optional | Built-in domain names to skip ("myco", "docs", "media"). |
| `domain` | `descriptor table` | optional | Inline descriptors nested as `[[domains.domain]]` — the flat `[[domain]]` spelling (\[`Config::domain`]) is the canonical form; both merge in declared order. |

## `[workspace]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `roots` | `Vec<PathBuf>` | optional | Sibling repo roots indexed together. |
| `resolve_git_deps` | `bool` | optional | Resolve `git = ".../org/repo"` manifest deps to siblings. |

## Constraints

* `deny_unknown_fields`: typos in field names fail the load.
* `extract.kinds` resolves to adapter crates (`manifest`,
  `treesitter`, `lsp`); unknown kinds warn at `kuda sync`.
* `summarize.kind` is `template` (default) or `acp`; `acp`
  requires `acp_cmd` and falls back to template on failure.

url: /kuda/reference/cards.md

# Reference: card schema

Two artifact files, both committed YAML under `.kuda/` (location
configurable via `[cards].dir`).

## `.kuda/index.yaml` — the L0 repo card

```yaml
name: kuda                     # repo display name
root: /abs/path/to/repo
purpose: ''                    # manifest/tagline — human-editable
modules:                       # sorted module names
- kuda-core
- kuda-store
commands:                      # detected verify/build commands
- cargo check
- cargo test --workspace
tree_digest: 93183a1c…         # sha1 over sorted path:hash lines —
                               # every walked file, one line
files_total: 12401             # walked-file count (diagnostic)
provenance:
  files: [Cargo.toml, crates/kuda-store/Cargo.toml, README.md]
  hashes: [sha1, ...]          # card inputs only: manifests + README
  commit_sha: af26b8c…
  generated_at: '1712345678'   # unix seconds
  generator: kuda/0.1.0
```

`provenance.files` on the L0 card is deliberately bounded —
manifests decide module identity, the README feeds `purpose`, and
`tree_digest`/`files_total` fingerprint the rest. Embedding the
full walked set put ~10k rows in the always-load card; per-file
hash lists still live on the L1 module cards where `status`
actually checks them.

## `.kuda/modules/<name>.yaml` — an L1 module card

```yaml
name: kuda-store
path: crates/kuda-store/Cargo.toml
purpose: Store port — IndexStore trait          # manifest description
api:                           # extracted public symbols — bounded:
- IndexStore                   # `_`-privates dropped, sorted, capped
- SqliteStore                  # at 40 entries
api_omitted: 217               # symbols beyond the cap ("+N more")
deps:                          # outgoing edges
- from: kuda-store
  to: kuda-core
  kind: PackageDep
notes: ''                      # HUMAN-OWNED — preserved on regen
verify:                        # files to open before trusting —
- crates/kuda-store/src/lib.rs # entry points first, capped at 10
provenance:
  files: [...]
  hashes: [...]
  commit_sha: …
  generated_at: '…'
  generator: kuda-template/0.1.0
```

## Provenance semantics

`files` + `hashes` are git `hash-object` digests of the card's
inputs at sync time. `kuda status` (and `mimus audit`) re-hash
the same files and compare — a mismatch marks the card `drifted`.
`commit_sha` records the index point in history; `generator`
records which adapter produced the card so format drift is
auditable.

## Ownership

Machine fields (`api`, `deps`, `provenance`, `purpose`) are
regenerated whenever a module drifts — `purpose` comes from the
domain descriptor → manifest description → crate docs → README
chain (or the `acp` agent's prose), so a hand-edit survives only
until the module's inputs change. `notes:` is the one
human-owned region: `carry_notes` copies the committed card's
notes forward verbatim on every regen — agent-suggested notes
land only when the committed region was empty.

# Explanation: architecture

kuda answers one question — *"what does this project look like,
right now, in a form an agent can load?"* — and treats a wrong
answer as worse than none.

## Where it sits

The org stack is **delivery → memory → process → interface**.
kuda is a **memory-layer organism**: a deterministic, repo-local tool
with a CLI and wire surfaces, no hosted state. It sits alongside
`myco` in memory, is audited by `mimus` (the falsifier in the
process layer), consumes `sturn`'s WAL as a provenance source when
present, and is consumed *by* the layers above — process
(`peregrin` campaigns), interface (`pavo` views), and delivery
(`tamias-driver-kuda` for distribution).

## The pipeline

```
repos ──► extract ──► summarize ──► index ──► store ──► serve
          │             │            │         │         │
   adapters:        adapters:    graph +   sqlite    cli |
   manifest         template     cards    + yaml    mcp | acp
   treesitter/       | acp        provenance
   lsp/records      (llm parked)
```

**Extract** is mechanical — no model, fully rerunnable. It pulls
symbols, package structure, and import edges.

**Summarize** turns each module's extraction into an L1 card —
committed YAML humans review in diffs.

**Index** merges everything into the symbol/dependency graph with
per-node provenance.

**Serve** is read-side only: `find`, `dependents`, `refs`,
`card`, `map`, `status` — plus the MCP and ACP wire surfaces.

## The tiers of memory

* **L0 repo card** (`.kuda/index.yaml`) — the ~1k-token
  always-load blob: purpose, module map, commands, provenance.
* **L1 module cards** (`.kuda/modules/*.yaml`) — fetched on
  demand when planning touches a module.
* **L1 file cards** (`.kuda/files/<module>/*.yaml`) — per-source-file
  `purpose` written by the semantic tier (opt-in,
  `[summarize] file_cards = true`). Files are chunked with a
  code-aware splitter (tree-sitter boundaries via text-splitter),
  fed to the agent, and hash-gated per file.
* **L2 graph** (`.kuda/index.sqlite`) — symbols, edges both
  directions, per-file hashes; gitignored, rebuildable, the query
  substrate.
* **L3** — the source itself. Memory is an index *into* code,
  never a replacement.

Committed L0/L1 + ignored L2 is deliberate: cards are reviewed
prose, the graph is derived state.

## Incremental sync

`sync` is diff-driven end to end:

1. One walk groups manifests + source files by module (manifest
   package names, not dir names — `kuda-docs`, not `docs`).
2. Every file gets an in-process git blob hash — no subprocess
   per file.
3. Hashes are compared against the store's `files` table —
   unchanged modules are never re-parsed; a changed file re-parses
   only its own module.
4. Cards whose provenance matches are reused verbatim — the
   summarizer (and the agent, in `acp` mode) is only invoked for
   drift.

Steady-state on a warm index is sub-second; agent spend is
per-drift, never per-sync. Deleted files and vanished modules are
detected by the same diff — their cards and store rows are
removed.

## Extraction tiers

Best-available wins, configured per repo via `[extract].kinds`:

* `manifest` — free, no parser: package graph + module
  boundaries from Cargo.toml/package.json/pyproject/go.mod.
* `treesitter` — grammar+query data from `data/langs/*`:
  symbols and `use`/import edges in ~any language.
* `lsp` — `documentSymbol` against a real server
  (`lsp_server = "rust-analyzer"`); the strongest signal where a
  server exists. Absent server = silent skip.

See [adding a language](../how-to/languages.md) — knowledge lives
in descriptor files; adding one is a data change.

## Language as data

Per-language knowledge — grammar refs, symbol queries, manifest
names — lives in `data/langs/*`, not in extractor code. The
adapters' vocabulary (`language()` registries, `SymbolKind`,
`EdgeKind`) is the only fixed part.

## Ports and adapters

`kuda-core` holds domain types only (`Symbol`, `ModuleCard`,
`Provenance`, `Claim`-free config). Every concern is a trait
crate + adapter crates:

* `kuda-extract` → `kuda-extract-manifest`, `kuda-extract-treesitter`,
  `kuda-extract-lsp`, `kuda-records` (non-code corpora)
* `kuda-store` → `kuda-store-sqlite`
* `kuda-summarize` → `kuda-template`, `kuda-acp` (`llm` parked)
* `kuda-config` → scarab-config-file discovery
  (`kuda.{yaml,yml,toml}`); `kuda-secret` → `kuda-keyring`,
  `kuda-dotenv` (no shipped consumer today)
* git access rides the shared `lasius-vcs` port
  (`lasius-vcs-git`) — there is no kuda-local vcs adapter

New capability = new adapter crate, not a core rewrite.

## Trust model

Every artifact carries `provenance {files, hashes, commit_sha,
generator}` — `kuda status` re-hashes and reports drift per card.
Cards end with `verify:` — the files an agent should open before
acting on the card. Memory is a hypothesis that narrows the
search space; the code remains the only truth. `mimus audit`
independently re-verifies card provenance — memory with an
external falsifier.

See [Boundaries](boundaries.md) for owns / does-not-own.

---

---
url: /kuda/explanation/boundaries.md
---
# Boundaries

kuda owns **repo memory** — extraction, cards, the symbol graph,
freshness. It does not own:

* **Verification** — `mimus` audits the cards; kuda emits claims,
  never verdicts.
* **Distribution** — the `kuda` command is a tamias pack
  (`libraries/kuda`); tamias owns install/transport.
* **Orchestration** — campaigns and scheduling are peregrin's;
  kuda exposes ops, never workflows.
* **Secrets** — credentials resolve through `kuda-secret` ports
  (keyring/dotenv); kuda never stores values.

---

---
url: /kuda/explanation/concepts.md
---
# Concepts

kuda's vocabulary is small but load-bearing — most of it is about
*what a card is allowed to claim*.

## Entity

* **Repo** — the unit of indexing. One `.kuda/` per checkout.
* **Workspace** — a set of sibling repo roots declared in
  `.kuda/workspace.yaml` (the only place `roots` is read);
  `[workspace] resolve_git_deps` in `kuda.toml` is a separate,
  config-file knob. Enables cross-repo queries like
  `dependents`.
* **Module** — the unit a card describes. Grouped by *manifest
  package name*, not directory name, so `kuda-docs/` (the `docs`
  worktree) indexes as `kuda-docs`, not `docs`.
* **File** — the unit of freshness. Every source file gets a git
  blob hash; a card's `verify:` list names the files an agent must
  open before trusting it.

## Memory tiers

* **L0 — repo card** (`.kuda/index.yaml`): the always-load blob.
  Purpose, module map, commands, provenance. ~1k tokens.
* **L1 — module cards** (`.kuda/modules/*.yaml`): fetched on
  demand when planning touches a module.
* **L1 file cards** (`.kuda/files/<module>/*.yaml`): per-source-file
  purpose, opt-in via `[summarize] file_cards = true`.
* **L2 — graph** (`.kuda/index.sqlite`): symbols, dependency edges
  both directions, per-file hashes. Gitignored, rebuildable —
  derived state, never reviewed prose.
* **L3 — the source**: the only truth. Memory is an index *into*
  code, never a replacement.

## Provenance

Every card carries `{files, hashes, commit_sha, generator}`.
`kuda status` re-hashes and reports drift per card — staleness is
a diff, not a guess. Cards are committed so humans review them in
git diffs; the L2 graph is ignored because it regenerates.

## Ports

* **extract** — mechanical symbol/edge pull. Adapters:
  `manifest` (package graph, free), `treesitter` (grammar+query
  data), `lsp` (a real language server, strongest where present),
  `records` (non-code corpora via domain descriptors).
* **summarize** — extraction → card prose. `template` is the
  deterministic default; `acp` delegates prose to an agent;
  `llm` is parked.
* **store** — where cards and the graph live (`sqlite` today).
* **vcs** — not a kuda port: commit-sha and blob-hash provenance
  go through the shared `lasius-vcs` port (git CLI impl).

## Surfaces

`kuda` CLI for humans and scripts; `kuda mcp` for MCP-speaking
agents; `kuda acp` to drive an external agent as the summarizer.
All read the same `.kuda/` artifacts.

---

---
url: /kuda/explanation/decisions.md
---
# Decisions

ADR-lite — the decisions that shape kuda, the alternatives
rejected, and the consequence each carries. Full history lives in
git and the org ledger (`project/`).

## Cards are committed; the graph is not

**Decision:** L0/L1 YAML cards are committed artifacts reviewed in
diffs; the L2 sqlite graph is gitignored and rebuildable.

**Alternatives:** commit everything (the graph churns every sync —
noise that drowns the prose); commit nothing (cards become
derived state nobody reviews, and provenance stops meaning
anything).

**Consequence:** cards are *claims with evidence* — humans and
`mimus audit` can falsify them. The graph is free to be a cache.

## Modules group by manifest package, not directory

**Decision:** extraction groups source files by the package name
declared in `Cargo.toml`/`package.json`/`pyproject.toml`, falling
back to directories only when no manifest exists.

**Alternatives:** directory grouping (splits one crate across
`src/`, `tests/`, `benches/` into fake "modules" and merges
unrelated dirs that happen to share a parent); repo-wide flat
indexing (no module boundary = no place to hang an L1 card).

**Consequence:** `docs/` (a git worktree) indexes as its own
package `kuda-docs`; workspace members stay distinct even when
they share a directory tree.

## Language knowledge is data, not code

**Decision:** per-language grammars, symbol queries, and manifest
names live in `data/langs/*`; extractor code only knows the
adapter vocabulary (`SymbolKind`, `EdgeKind`).

**Alternatives:** per-language extractor crates (a release per
language, adapter sprawl); tree-sitter-only (no package-graph
signal — the free `manifest` tier disappears).

**Consequence:** adding a language is a data change reviewable in
a diff — see [adding a language](../how-to/languages.md). The cost
is a small descriptor DSL the extractors must interpret.

## Sync is hash-gated end to end

**Decision:** every file gets an in-process git blob hash compared
against the store; unchanged modules are never re-parsed and cards
with matching provenance are reused verbatim — including skipping
the summarizer/agent entirely.

**Alternatives:** mtime-based staleness (unreliable across
checkouts and rebases); always-resummarize (agent spend per sync
instead of per drift).

**Consequence:** steady-state sync is sub-second and agent spend
scales with *change*, not repo size. The `files` table in sqlite
is the source of truth for "did this file change."

## Releases are tag-only; the command is a tamias pack

**Decision:** releases run `tarsi-serve release --dir .` directly
— bump, tag, push, no publish targets (`tarsi.toml` disables
crates.io and GitHub Releases); the per-repo `scripts/release.sh`
shim was removed org-wide. The `kuda` command
ships as the `libraries/kuda` tamias pack; `kuda-cli` is lib-only.

**Alternatives:** crates.io + cargo-dist binaries; a `[[bin]]`
in `kuda-cli`; release-plz/GHA (hosted CI for a project whose
point is that CI is a local loop).

**Consequence:** one version across the workspace, one tag scheme,
and install/update lifecycle owned by tamias — but there is no
`cargo install kuda`, and pack publishing stays a manual
credentials-gated step. See [the release model](release-model.md).

---

---
url: /kuda/explanation/release-model.md
---
# The release model

Releases are **tag-only** — there is no crates.io publish and no
GitHub Releases artifact. `kuda`'s crates are lib-only engines;
the user-facing command is the tamias pack in `libraries/kuda`.

## The flow

Releases are operator-run: `tarsi-serve release --dir .` talks to
[`tarsi-serve`](https://9aia.com/tarsi/) — the org release plane
(project ADR-0005) — directly; the per-repo `scripts/release.sh`
shim was removed org-wide. One call runs plan → changelog → bump →
tag → push; `tarsi-serve release` is dry-run by default and
`--yes` is the explicit opt-in.

Repo policy lives in `tarsi.toml`:

* `[publish.crates] enabled = false` — crates.io publishing is
  tamias-only (ADR-0004).
* `[publish.ghreleases] enabled = false` — org releases are
  tag-only; the capability stays for opt-in.
* `[release.sync_refs]` rewrites `libraries/kuda/tamias.yaml`'s
  `version:` and the README's `kuda@<ver>` install ref inside the
  release commit, so the tagged tree is self-consistent.

Units default to cargo workspace members; versions are
workspace-inherited, so releasing units share one bump.

## Shipping the command

Tagging doesn't publish anything user-facing. The pack ships
manually:

```sh
scripts/pack.sh                                # stage driver payload
#   → release-builds tamias-driver-kuda into
#     libraries/kuda/drivers/bin/<triple>/ (gitignored)
tamias publish libraries/kuda                  # → 9aia:kuda@<ver>
```

Install is then `tamias install 9aia:kuda@<ver>`
(needs `TAMIAS_REGISTRY_TOKEN`) or
`tamias install --allow-drivers ./libraries/kuda`
from a checkout.

## Why this shape

* **Tag-only + pack publish** matches the org distribution
  model: git/tag deps and the tamias registry are the channels;
  crates.io and GitHub Releases stay unused.
* **tarsi over bespoke scripts**: plan/changelog/bump/tag is the
  same pipeline every org repo runs — the repo keeps only policy
  (`tarsi.toml`), not machinery.
* **`dist-workspace.toml` is configured but idle** — prebuilt
  binary distribution (cargo-dist + GitHub Releases) remains a
  possible future option, not part of the release flow.

url: /kuda/comparison.md
---
# kuda vs the alternatives

## vs grep + re-read every session

|                       | grep/ripgrep          | kuda                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------- |
| find a symbol         | fast, per-query       | fast — plus kind + card    |
| "what depends on X"   | manual, cross-repo pain | one query                |
| overall comprehension | none                  | L0 card in ~1k tokens      |
| freshness             | always current        | provenance-checked         |
| doc/comment mentions  | same grep             | unified `refs --docs`      |

## vs embeddings / RAG

|                       | RAG store             | kuda                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------- |
| fuzzy semantic lookup | strong                | (optional store adapter later)|
| dep graph, provenance | weak                  | first-class                |
| staleness             | opaque                | explicit sha/hash diff     |
| determinism           | model-dependent       | `template` = deterministic |

## vs LSP alone

|                       | LSP                   | kuda                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------- |
| cross-file refs       | strong (per language) | `lsp` adapter reuses them     |
| needs a running server| yes                   | only for the `lsp` tier    |
| prose/cards           | none                  | L1/L0 artifacts            |
| persistence           | session-scoped        | committed + rebuildable    |

Trade-off: kuda adds an index step and committed artifacts — the
payoff is that "overall comprehension" becomes a fixed ~1k-token
load instead of a per-session expedition.
